items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: He's running a fever. Someone help get this man up on the table.

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: There's medicine in the box, the white one. Mr. Becket, boil some more water, prepare a damp towel!
After receiving the call, the doctor hurries over, attending to the sick tramp in the diner.

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: Dr. Liu, I'm guessing this fella can't foot the bill for this, and we might not be able to front it for him neither.

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: There's an old saying where I'm from, Becket.

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: "Saving a life is greater than building a seven-tiered pagoda." Saving lives is what matters.

items.speaker: Hollick
items.text: A pagoda, is that like a cake or something?

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: It's a kind of building, gentlemen. Now, if you're wasting time thinking of layer cakes, how about you come over here and help out with dishes instead?
On the other side of the diner, the group is still busily cooking and distributing food.

items.speaker: Eternity
items.text: Hold on, this is less than what you gave the people before me, what's up?

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Pardon, Ms. Eternity, but we're forced by necessity to distribute what we have based on each individual's situation.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Frankly, ma'am, there are people here that have gone days without a proper meal, and with you in that fetching blue dress ...

items.speaker: Sputnik
items.text: Mr. Pioneer, it would be best for you to speak less and work more.
In the corner, two little girls have rummaged through Eternity's handbag, pulling out an assortment of curious trinkets, sprawling them out on the floor to play with.

items.speaker: Eternity
items.text: Hmm?

items.speaker: Eternity
items.text: Oh! Darlings, didn't your parents teach you not to take other people's things? Be good little dears and return those to me.

items.speaker: Street Kid
items.text: Parents?
There's no one around them, and no one speaks up for them.

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: These kids are either from the orphanage or raised on the streets like us, grabbing whatever grub they can.

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: Haha, you remember Paulina? J's sis, tight with cash but big-hearted, spitting image of him when she was young.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Miss Paulina found herself a respectable job somewhere beyond this place. I'm so happy for her—happy and proud.

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: I'm happy for any kid that makes it out of Haight Street.

items.speaker: Hollick
items.text: You've gotta be!

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: Let's quit all this racket, Hollick. You go on and grab some blankets for these folks.
Eternity shifts the children's hands from the old toys, leading them by their sauce-stained fingers toward the makeshift beds.

items.speaker: Eternity
items.text: If you behave, with no crying or fussing, I'll give you two chocolate candies. How about that, my little lambs?
The little lambs nod.
Eternity's royal blue blanket wraps them into a slumber—warm and sheltered from the elements and hunger.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Alright, gents, time to tidy up. Clear some space, clean the utensil. Then tonight we're hosting a San Francisco story time!

items.speaker: Sputnik
items.text: Did you—Did you hear something outside just now? The sound of brakes, maybe?

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Perhaps the radio waves disrupted you, Ms. Sputnik. They were adjusting the TV antenna earlier.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: This the place, Antony?

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: He's gotta be here.
The turncoat has brought his new allies straight to his former hangout.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: You best not screw this up. The boss is still sore about last time.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: You swore on your mama's life, but then you let him get away.

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: Well, I didn't count on him bailing over a rooftop, but in case you didn't know this diner of his ain't about to sprout legs and run.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: I got my GED. Don't play me for a chump! So, what if he ain't here?

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: Not possible. Bruno tipped me off—said J's back at the diner, playing saint to the homeless.

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: So believe me or not, but how can you doubt our friendly neighborhood copper?

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: Anyway, let's kick this off with a bang!

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: I'll go in with one of the guys, the rest of you stay put. No need to rattle the cage just yet.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: Sounds like you're trying to make yourself into the next boss.
The ill-intentioned old friend, with his vicious dog in tow, heads straight into the diner.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Apologies, gentlemen, we can't serve you today. The diner's closed.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Antony?

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: Who? Antony?!

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Oh, I seem to recall your hulking, ill-tempered friend from before.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: Where's J?
At this moment, he is likely rushing down some San Francisco avenue, having just missed his would-be target.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: If you're looking for the person in charge here, I can temporarily stand in for our absent acting manager, and discuss matters with you. What do you need?

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: A talking dummy? What the heck's a dummy doin' in a diner? Hahaha, look, Antony! It freaking talks!

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: All that aside, sir. Let me be clear, I am J's representative while he's out. So, whatever your issues, please bring them up to me.

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: Hollick, keep those tongs handy. We got company.

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: We gotta be good hosts, don't we?

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: I wouldn't recommend getting handsy, Becket.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: You wanna throw down again, lil' buddy?
The bald muscle blocks Antony's path, fists clenched, eyeing the occupants of the diner.
Fear, disgust, contempt, and curiosity.

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: Let's take this outside, to the corner. We don't want people thinkin' Ol' Tang Ji's in any trouble now.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: We're here, and we ain't leaving. Now, where's that coward hiding? Has he gone chicken and fled the coop?

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: I'm thinking we nickname him "Chicken Head" from now on! Haight Street's Rooster J—sounds good, don't it? Hahaha!
Some laugh awkwardly, while most remain silent.

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: If you've got a shred of decency, not for J's sake, but for Tang Ji's, you'll step outside with us.
Wild dogs don't fight in their own den. That's the rule of the streets.

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: Fine. Let's take this outside.
Becket and Hollick, one with a steel pipe, the other gripping long metal tongs, follow the towering enforcer outside with Antony.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Gents, please keep your cool. Let's try to talk this out. No need for fists.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Isn't it always best to avoid a scrap?
The mannequin man pleads as he likes, but he knows his friends' temperaments. Cooler heads will not prevail.

items.speaker: Eternity
items.text: Oh, this is more thrilling than any prime-time soap opera.

items.speaker: Eternity
items.text: Still, children shouldn't see such unwholesome scenes.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: So, where's that punk hiding?

items.speaker: Hollick
items.text: Hiding! Haha, the boss is out there right now looking for you, you little rat!

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: Looking for me? Yeah, right! I'm the one trying to track him down!

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: What's the deal? You promised that this chicken would be holed up in the diner.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: So where's he at?!
By sheer coincidence, it seems they've chosen to time their raids for the very same moment.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: If you ask me, we oughta yank a couple of teeth out and get the truth on that jerk straight from their mouths.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: What, you going soft?

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: Can it! Or did you not remember what the boss told us?

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: "Use your head more than your fists."

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: "If this can be handled clean, then don't go makin' it ugly."

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: "We're all businessmen here—businessmen who know the rules."

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: So let's not make things ugly. Mull over a little "ren qing si gu," you got it?

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: Hmph.
Antony turns to face his former friends with a sly vulpine smile.

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: Becket, ol' pal-o-mine, a top-notch mechanic like you oughta have your own shop by now, dontcha think?

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: We go way back. Remember our time in the joint?

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: I don't remember nothing.

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: But I do know you're an ungrateful rat.

items.speaker: Hollick
items.text: Yeah, a rat!
It seems like they aren't buying his false smile.
Antony's honeyed words are met with a thick gob of spit sent straight to his face.

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: Right, J, he's been good to me, like a real brother. But his sister—with her nose always up in the air like that?

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: She thinks we're just slum dogs, too filthy to even say hello.

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: Sure, J's got enough grub for everyone, but with his act, he ain't ever striking it rich.
Striking it rich.
Now he really is just another lap dog from Grant Ave.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: Stop dragging this out.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: Whatever you and your little circus got going on ain't none of my concern, but we can't head back with nada.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: Snatch those two. If J's MIA, we'll nab his little buddies and snap off some parts till he shows up!
The henchman calls out, and a group of almost clone-like thugs in black rush out from the van, seizing the two companions.

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: Hollick!

items.speaker: Hollick
items.text: Where the hell did all these—!
Hollick and Becket, though outnumbered, still attempt to resist, but in a few swift moves, they are bound up and hoisted into the back of the van, becoming "spoils of war."

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: Take 'em to the club, into the freezer, oh no, the basement! We'll sort 'em out later!

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: You look like you've packed on a couple more pounds.
The stray dog eyes his former companions, as his "new friends" busily tie the two captives on either side of an oil drum.

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: Strap 'em in real tight, especially that twig Becket. He's slippery. Give him an inch and he'll escape.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: Don't worry, we'll have someone on the door.

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: Alright, just keep it clean for the boss. He's got some big shots coming by tomorrow night, so get your A-team on this—we're on tonight.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: You're getting ahead of yourself, lil' pup. You're just a mutt the boss took in, and now you think you get to run the show?

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: A mutt? Pfft! A mutt's way more loyal than this backstabber!

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: Who told you to speak?

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: Hold up! Smacking them around ain't helping nobody. Just make sure they get some grub later; the boss might still need 'em.

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: I'm headed upstairs. The crowd's really rolling in. Watch the place. No drama tonight.

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: Man, can you shift your fat rear a smidge to the left.

items.speaker: Hollick
items.text: I can't move a thing.

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: J's been harping on about slimming down, hitting the gym, and you never took the hint?!

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: That lowlife Antony.

items.speaker: Hollick
items.text: What's the game plan now, bro?

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: The game plan? We keep our wits sharp, get some shut-eye. Trust J. For now, zip it, and wait for that rat Antony to drop off some grub.

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: We won't be any good without some chow. J'll get us. He'll make it. Don't stress bro!
J has never failed them before, and as far as Becket's concerned, he never will.
West Coast Star
The West Coast Star, a shrine to Bacchus in the heart of San Francisco.

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: I got this hunch, man, like we might see some action here tonight.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: Got your eye on one of the new chicks?

items.speaker: Antony
items.text: Nah, more like a dude, a young one. Yeah, man, it's always the young guns stirring up trouble.
Hearing this, the burly enforcer raises his eyebrow, casting a strange glance at Antony.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: You into that scene? Cool, I mean, this city is all about freedom.
In the neon glow, all tastes find refuge. As the night flows, all manner of whispers and desires mingle here—
Whispers of the second millennium's end, as the soothsayer's murmurings of the "apocalypse of 1999" approach ... for now the people revel!
